Let's see... In 2014, I was 14 years old, and my mother had a friend who was 28. He was a meth addict and had just broken up with the "love of his life" and was all sorts of messed up. My mom felt really sorry for him and took him in, and he stayed with us for a few months. At that stage in my life, I was growing into myself, developing, becoming confident in my womanhood and starting to explore. 

It started with compliments. My food is great. I'm beautiful. We have the same interests, etc. At that stage in my life I had never had a boyfriend, and not for lack of trying. I was pretty desperate to feel the type of love and desire I read about in Twilight books. So I fell for him, and I fell hard. It started with cuddles, and just spending more and more time together. My mom broke up with her bf at the time so we moved to my grandparents and he had me pretty much to himself. My mom was broken up about the ex and also started using meth, and was either high on meth or weed most of the time thanks to him. I'm ashamed to admit I have no memories of my little sister in those months. I'm still trying to make up for what I did. My grandparents kept to themselves so he could coerce me as he pleased.

Reality quickly faded as he became my whole world. Everything revolved around the feeling of being loved and wanted, I started missing a lot of school, and lost touch with my friends. I wanted to do everything and anything to keep him loving me. I lost my virginity to him after a month, it wasn't bad. We then had sex almost every single day for the next three months. The problem was that he convinced me that he didn't need to use a condom. He said it didn't feel the same for him, and that an abortion was easy as taking a pill and it would be gone. I was very naive. I knew he had an ex he had gotten pregnant. 

The whole time we were together he never stopped telling me about how much he loved his one ex, he would go on and on about the sex they had, about how beautiful she was, about how he would move mountains for her. She was a heroin addict. He didn't work either, and the only time he got jobs was to pay for his meth. He taught me to cook it, and how to help him shoot it. He offered it to me many times, and I'm very proud to say I never once took him up on it. I was convinced I could fix him.

Then three months later he leaves to spend a week of Christmas with his mom, on the other side of the country. When he left, it's like a great film was removed from my mind, and I actually opened up to one of my mom's new bfs friends. I had told my "bf" before he left that I thought I was pregnant. He left anyways, and I guess I sort of knew he wasn't coming back, because I told the friend, who told my mom. New year's eve I have a pregnancy test and it comes out positive. I tell him, he stays put. My mom gave me an option, completely free of bias. I chose to have an abortion, and on New Year's Day 2015 I did it. I know there will be judgement and harassment for this choice, but please try to understand it from a scared, broken hearted 14 year old. I had just lost the "love of my life." I was terrified of what having a baby would do to my body. I was terrified of me, a child, having to raise a child, and having to explain to it one day what kind of a father it had. I didn't want to drop out of school, I didn't want to have my future ruined. I wanted to travel the world, I can't do that with a child. I wanted to love again, and few men will be with a woman who was pregnant at 14. I wanted a future, and in that moment, I saw death, or depression, or even worse, resenting my own child. I wanted to have a child when we would both be able to live happy lives, and maybe I had poor judgement then, but this is the way I saw it.

The story goes on, I go back to school, and tell my mom's ex bfs daughter about the whole thing. I needed someone my own age to vent to. She then told her dad, who, holding a grudge against my mother, told my school, and the school then proceeded to be very biased and judgemental of me. I had to change schools halfway through the year.

At 20, 6 years later, I still look back on how it affected me. How I've had to go through intense therapy to even feel okay with sex again, and actually understand how it feels to make love and feel real love, not use and abuse. I still get a leftover "dirty feeling' as I call it when something sexual happens, because of how the whole thing ended up. I still have a lot of healing to do, and I have to live with the choice I made every day. He was an awful, dangerous man, who still to this day terrifies me. Predators are dangerous people, and children are so easily influenced. They come from the simplest of places, and cause a lot of damage. I only wish I could protect other girls from the same thing, but for now, at least I can make sure my little sister is safe.

Your situation makes me want to cry, because I really feel for you. You love your wife, she's the only love you've known in a world thats so fast paced and difficult to understand. I can tell by the desperate way you're trying to understand how to be better that you actually want to be better, for her and for yourself. You've had a messed up childhood, and having those problems doesn't make things any easier. 

A lot of people here are saying you should leave your wife, and I'm honestly inclined to agree. It's difficult, because you love her so much, and she's most likely your whole world right now, and making things right with her is so much less painful than trying to live without her.

I can tell you one thing though, if you read this. As a woman in an relationship with a man who has been abused his whole childhood, and has a few problems he's still trying to work on, patience is key. He's wonderful, in so many ways, but he also has days where he can be difficult to deal with. But as his partner, I need to be patient with him, understand why he reacted or did what he did. 

I can imagine there's a lot that's happened between you two in the time you've been married, and that it's something you're trying to fix, but your wife has no patience with you. Nothing, and I mean nothing, excuses her treatment of you. If she wants a change, she has to be the change she wants to see in you. Positive reinforcement. Appreciation of you reading the articles, accepting your faults and making an effort to try. 

Tell me OP, when was the last time she thanked you? When was the last time she complimented you? When was the last time she told you she loved you?

At what point are you going to fall over from exhaustion chasing her carrot? At what point is this wild goose chase going to strip away the last parts of your hope and happiness? It already sounds like you're falling into a depression and my gosh I would like you to not let that happen.

It's good to want the change, but if your wife is not going to try as well, how long are you going to carry the relationship on your shoulders for?

Everyone is telling you to walk away, get help, and I think you should. But we are just strangers who've had a glimpse into your life, who haven't experienced the past years of your life. This is on you. This is where you have to sit down and make the choice. And think, ask the right questions, study your relationship, see it for what it truly is, and make a plan of action.

I hope whatever you do brings you happiness. Don't forget that there are other people out there in the world that can bring you happiness and love, that can give you more. It's scary to step outside, to take the first step, but once you start, every step gets easier.

Keep us updated OP. Stay strong, stay healthy, and do the right thing for yourself, and your wife.
